title.value: Adjusting Machine Learning Decisions for Equal Opportunity and Counterfactual Fairness
title.justification: This value is the exact title of the paper as listed in the information provided.
title.quote: Adjusting Machine Learning Decisions for Equal Opportunity and Counterfactual Fairness

extractions.description: The paper discusses two algorithms that adjust fitted Machine Learning (ML) predictors to produce fair decisions, specifically focusing on fairness in high-stakes decisions, such as bail admissions or credit lending. By defining fairness through equal counterfactual opportunity and counterfactual fairness criteria, the authors propose methods that do not require retraining the ML models. The algorithms are evaluated on datasets concerning admissions, income, credit, and recidivism, showing trade-offs between fairness and accuracy.

climate_change_is_central.justification: Climate Change is not a central theme of this paper. The paper focuses on fairness in machine learning, particularly in contexts like admissions and risk assessments, without mention of sustainability or environmental impacts.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Machine learning (ml) methods have the potential to automate high-stakes decisions, such as bail admissions or credit lending, by analyzing and learning from historical data.

primary_category.justification: The paper is focused on fairness in machine learning, particularly counterfactual fairness in high-stakes decision processes, and does not directly address any climate change issues.
primary_category.quote: ...we develop two methods that adjust existing ML decision-makers to produce algorithmic decisions that are both accurate and fair.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not touch upon secondary Climate Change themes as it is entirely focused on fairness in machine learning.
